title: Engineering Measures to Reduce Flash Floods at Bukit Timah Canal and Ulu Pandan Canal Areas
what_it_is: Engineering Measures to Reduce Flash Floods at Bukit Timah Canal and Ulu Pandan Canal Areas

sections.label: April 2021 Sumatra squall rainfall
sections.summary: On 17 April 2021, a Sumatra squall and typhoon-influenced winds caused intense rain, with Ulu Pandan recording 170.6 millimetres, the highest April daily rainfall since 1980.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, on 17 April 2021, the Sumatra squall, coupled with convergence of surrounding winds arising from the influence of typhoon "Surigae" near the Philippines gave rise to intense and prolonged rainfall across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The highest rainfall that day was at Ulu Pandan with 170.6 millimetres of rain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This is the highest daily rainfall recorded in April since 1980 and is equivalent to 110% of Singapore’s average rainfall for the whole month of April, falling in a single day.

sections.label: Bukit Timah Road flash floods
sections.summary: High canal water levels impeded discharge, causing flash floods of about 150 millimetres on Dunearn and Bukit Timah Roads that subsided within 30 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The water levels in Bukit Timah Canal were very high due to the intense and prolonged rain, impeding discharge from roadside drains along Dunearn Road and Bukit Timah Road into the canal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This resulted in floods of around 150-millimetre depth at Dunearn and Bukit Timah Roads, and around 50-millimetre depth on the pedestrian sidewalks adjacent to the roadside drains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: All affected roads remained passable to traffic and the flash floods subsided within 30 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Public Utilities Board (PUB) had completed the upgrading of the Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal – this is the stretch marked in blue – between Bukit Timah Road and Clementi Road in September 2019 at a project cost of $300 million to alleviate flood risks along Bukit Timah Road and Dunearn Road.

sections.label: Remaining Bukit Timah Canal upgrading
sections.summary: PUB started upgrading the remaining Bukit Timah Canal section between Rifle Range Road and Jalan Kampong Chantek, expected to complete in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: PUB started the upgrading work on the remaining section of Bukit Timah Canal between Rifle Range Road and Jalan Kampong Chantek – this is the stretch marked in red – where the localised flash flood occurred, and is expected to complete it in 2024.

sections.label: Government drainage and flood resilience spending
sections.summary: Since 2011 the Government invested almost $2 billion in drainage works and will invest another $1.4 billion over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Since 2011, the Government has invested almost $2 billion in drainage works and will invest another $1.4 billion over the next five years to enhance our flood resilience.
